requirements.evidence: Contract matches task: enum app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9 with the three string cases, NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:17). Queue re-read under lockForUpdate and is_active checked before any write (CallNextTicket.php:22-30). Ordering is priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc (:112); normal_only/fairness use oldest first (:110). Fairness takes the last 3 called by called_at desc, id desc, needs count === 3, all priority > 0, and a waiting normal (:74-90), and only applies in Any mode (:31). Candidates are locked one by one and re-checked as waiting, with losers skipped (:43-59). Writes only status/called_at/called_by_user_id and returns the refreshed model (:53-58). Throws when nothing is eligible (:35-37, :61). One small risk: the fairness history filters on status = Called (:76), so it would miss tickets that later move to another status, if such statuses exist.

conventions.evidence: The domain write lives in app/Actions as one invokable class per use case, with no service or repository layer. No authorization, as the task allows. Updates both docs/business-rules.md (new 'Call the next ticket' paragraph, scope notes adjusted) and docs/architecture.md ('Call the next ticket' section now names the implementation and links the test, and the TODO is removed). CHANGELOG.md gets an entry under Added. Uses Pest feature tests with RefreshDatabase and factories, like the other tests. Test-first order can't be checked from a diff.

security.evidence: No HTTP or Livewire surface. The task says the caller is trusted, so no authorization is expected. Writes use direct attribute assignment and save() (CallNextTicket.php:53-56), so there is no mass assignment and the model's write-once updating hook still runs. Row locks on the queue and the candidate prevent double calls (:22-25, :44-47).

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php has 16 tests covering: ordering and the id tie-break (:23-58), queue/status isolation (:60-78), both restricted modes (:80-101), fairness tripped, no normal waiting, and streak reset (:103-178), inactive and stale-inactive queues with no change (:201-223), the three no-eligible cases (:225-246), and the returned model's fields (:248-264). Gaps: the skip-on-concurrently-called path (CallNextTicket.php:49-51) is never exercised. The test 'ignores fairness in priority_only and normal_only modes. (:180) only tests priority_only. The last test compares $called->fresh() with $ticket->fresh(), which is the same row, so that assertion can't fail.

simplicity.evidence: Lean design: two small private helpers and no speculative abstraction. The NormalOnly/restrictToNormal condition appears twice (CallNextTicket.php:104 and :108) when one branch would do. The action repeats the status/called_at/called_by_user_id assignment instead of reusing Ticket::call(). That can be justified, because Ticket::call() throws on non-waiting tickets and checks entity membership.

readability.evidence: Clear names (fairnessTripped, candidateIds, lockedQueue). Comments explain why: the stale queue instance at :20-21 and the exactly-once reasoning at :39-42. PHPDoc on the fairness helper and the Collection return type. Only nit: unused $issuedAt in the test file (:252).

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: action, enum, exception, tests, the two required docs and a CHANGELOG entry (the conventions require it). No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: No test exercises the skip-and-pick-next path when a candidate is no longer waiting after the lock, which is the exactly-once rule 7.

The fairness history is filtered by status = Called rather than by called_at being set, so tickets that later move to another status (e.g. served or skipped) would drop out of the last-3 window and change the fairness result.
The test name claims fairness is ignored in both priority_only and normal_only, but only priority_only is tested.

The test compares $called->fresh() with $ticket->fresh(), which load the same row, so it can't detect immutable fields changing. The original values should be captured before the call. $issuedAt is also unused.
The NormalOnly || restrictToNormal condition is evaluated twice; one if/elseif branch could set both the filter and the order.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action, the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, matching the contract. It covers deterministic ordering, the three modes, the 3-ticket fairness rule, the stale-safe inactive-queue check and exactly-once locking, and updates both docs and the CHANGELOG. The tests are thorough. The remaining gaps are small: no test for the concurrent-skip path, one weak assertion, and a fairness history keyed on the Called status, so I would approve with nits.
